Pikliz

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 8 as a condimentPrep 15 min

Pikliz is a spicy Haitian pickled vegetable relish made primarily of cabbage, carrots, and Scotch bonnet peppers. It is traditionally served during Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa, as a vibrant accompaniment symbolizing the earth's bounty and the fiery spirit of the farmer's hard work.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups shredded green cabbage (about 150 g)
  • 1 cup shredded carrots (about 120 g)
  • 1/2 cup thinly sliced white onion (about 60 g)
  • 2-3 Scotch bonnet peppers, thinly sliced (adjust for heat preference)
  • 1/4 cup white vinegar (60 ml)
  • 1/4 cup fresh lime juice (60 ml)
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon black peppercorns
  • 1/2 teaspoon whole cloves (optional)
  • 1/2 teaspoon whole allspice berries (optional)

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine the shredded cabbage, carrots, sliced onion, and Scotch bonnet peppers.
  2. In a separate small bowl, mix together the white vinegar, lime juice, and salt until the salt dissolves.
  3. Pour the vinegar mixture over the vegetables and toss well to combine.
  4. Add the black peppercorns, cloves, and allspice berries to the mixture.
  5. Transfer the mixture to a clean glass jar or airtight container, pressing down lightly to pack the vegetables.
  6. Seal the container and refrigerate for at least 24 hours before serving to allow flavors to meld.
  7. Serve chilled or at room temperature as a spicy, tangy condiment alongside grilled meats, rice dishes, or traditional Haitian meals during Fete de Papa Zaka.

Tips

  • Adjust the number of Scotch bonnet peppers to control the heat level.
  • For a milder version, remove the seeds from the peppers before slicing.
  • Pikliz can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks and often tastes better after a few days as the flavors develop.
